records.context: **high confidence, and wrong** — the model was sure. When a model that is right 95% of the time is *certain* about an object and disagrees with the annotation, the likeliest explanation is that the annotation is wrong. These are the extracted image regions to re-label.

records.source: **high confidence, and wrong** — the model was sure. When a model that is right 95% of the time is *certain* about an object and disagrees with the annotation, the likeliest explanation is that the annotation is wrong. These are the crops to re-label.
records.translation: **alta confianza, y equivocado**: el modelo estaba seguro. Cuando un modelo que acierta el 95% de las veces está *seguro* sobre un objeto y discrepa de la anotación, la explicación más probable es que la anotación sea errónea. Estos son los recortes que hay que volver a etiquetar.

records.context: **A cell is not a homogeneous population.** 43 errors spread evenly over 20 microplate sample positions is a model problem. 43 errors *all from well A01* is a staining problem, and re-labelling any of them is wasted work — the fix is upstream, at the bench. :func:`breakdown_by` and :func:`describe_breakdown` are that check, made before anyone opens a single extracted image region.

records.source: **A cell is not a homogeneous population.** 43 errors spread evenly over 20 wells is a model problem. 43 errors *all from well A01* is a staining problem, and re-labelling any of them is wasted work — the fix is upstream, at the bench. :func:`breakdown_by` and :func:`describe_breakdown` are that check, made before anyone opens a single crop.
records.translation: **Una celda no es una población homogénea.** 43 errores repartidos de manera uniforme entre 20 pocillos son un problema del modelo. 43 errores *todos del pocillo A01* son un problema de tinción, y volver a etiquetar cualquiera de ellos es trabajo perdido: la solución está antes, en el laboratorio. :func:`breakdown_by` y :func:`describe_breakdown` son esa comprobación, hecha antes de que nadie abra un solo recorte.

records.source: number of mutually exclusive classifier classes.

records.context: ``confidence`` is the probability of the class the model *chose*, so it can never fall below ``1 / n_classes`` — a two-class model is at 0.5 when it is maximally undecided, and a ten-class model is at 0.1. A fixed 0.5 would therefore call every ten-class error "high confidence" and every two-class error nothing at all, which is the sort of default that makes a feature look broken on somebody else's data.
records.label: spacr.confusion.confidence_threshold#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``confidence`` is the probability of the class the model *chose*, so it can never fall below ``1 / n_classes`` — a two-class model is at 0.5 when it is maximally undecided, and a ten-class model is at 0.1. A fixed 0.5 would therefore call every ten-class error "high confidence" and every two-class error nothing at all, which is the sort of default that makes a feature look broken on somebody else's data.
records.translation: ``confidence`` es la probabilidad de la clase que *eligió* el modelo, por lo que nunca puede caer por debajo de ``1 / n_classes``: un modelo de dos clases está en 0.5 cuando está totalmente indeciso, y uno de diez clases en 0.1. records.context: Comparisons can use cells, microplate sample positions, or laboratory microplates as observations. Statistical test selection is delegated to :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, and each result records its normality, equal-variance, and sample-size evidence. Cell-level tests treat individual cells as observations and do not account for cells that share a microplate sample position; use the microplate sample position level when microplate sample positions are the experimental units.
records.label: spacr.gene_measurement_compare#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Comparisons can use cells, wells, or plates as observations. Statistical test selection is delegated to :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, and each result records its normality, equal-variance, and sample-size evidence. Cell-level tests treat individual cells as observations and do not account for cells that share a well; use the well level when wells are the experimental units.
records.translation: Las comparaciones pueden usar células, pocillos o placas como observaciones. La selección de la prueba estadística se delega en :mod:`spacr.sp_stats`, y cada resultado registra sus pruebas de normalidad, de igualdad de varianzas y de tamaño muestral. Las pruebas a nivel de célula tratan las células individuales como observaciones y no tienen en cuenta las células que comparten un pocillo; use el nivel de pocillo cuando los pocillos sean las unidades experimentales.

records.source: All ten layouts encode the same six facts -- plate, well, field, channel, z, t -- and differ only in how. So rather than matching a whole filename against one of N templates, this module reads the parts of the name that vary across the folder and infers what each varying part means.
records.translation: Las diez disposiciones codifican los mismos seis datos (placa, pocillo, campo de imagen, canal, z, t) y solo difieren en cómo lo hacen. Por ello, en lugar de comparar un nombre de archivo completo con una de N plantillas, este módulo lee las partes del nombre que varían en la carpeta e infiere qué significa cada parte variable.

records.context: Variation across the folder identifies the axes. A token that is the same in every file carries no information: ``L01`` in ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` is a constant for the whole plate and identifies nothing. A token that takes two values across eight files is an axis with two positions. Only the folder, not a single filename, shows which tokens are axes.
records.label: spacr.image_import#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Variation across the folder identifies the axes. A token that is the same in every file carries no information: ``L01`` in ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` is a constant for the whole plate and identifies nothing. A token that takes two values across eight files is an axis with two positions. Only the folder, not a single filename, shows which tokens are axes.
records.translation: La variación en la carpeta identifica los ejes. Un segmento que es igual en todos los archivos no aporta información: ``L01`` en ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` es una constante para toda la placa y no identifica nada. Un segmento que toma dos valores en ocho archivos es un eje con dos posiciones. Solo la carpeta, y no un único nombre de archivo, muestra qué segmentos son ejes.

records.context: Markers identify which axis a varying token is. ``F001`` and ``C01`` both vary and are not interchangeable; the letter in front names the axis, and every convention in the corpus uses one. The marker table below is that vocabulary, and it is short because the conventions mostly share their letters.
records.label: spacr.image_import#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Markers identify which axis a varying token is. ``F001`` and ``C01`` both vary and are not interchangeable; the letter in front names the axis, and every convention in the corpus uses one. The marker table below is that vocabulary, and it is short because the conventions mostly share their letters.
records.translation: Los marcadores identifican a qué eje corresponde un segmento variable. ``F001`` y ``C01`` varían ambos y no son intercambiables; la letra que los precede nombra el eje, y todas las convenciones del corpus usan una. La tabla de marcadores siguiente es ese vocabulario, y es breve porque las convenciones comparten en su mayoría las mismas letras.

records.context: No role is assigned without evidence. A token that varies and carries no recognisable marker is reported as unplaced, with its values, so the caller can ask the user. A partly unparseable tree imports what it can and reports the rest, rather than returning a plausible but wrong answer; the older ``consolidate`` path instead lost images without an error.
records.label: spacr.image_import#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: No role is assigned without evidence. A token that varies and carries no recognisable marker is reported as unplaced, with its values, so the caller can ask the user. A partly unparseable tree imports what it can and reports the rest, rather than returning a plausible but wrong answer; the older ``consolidate`` path instead lost images without an error.
records.translation: No se asigna ningún rol sin pruebas. Un segmento que varía y no lleva ningún marcador reconocible se notifica como no ubicado, con sus valores, para que quien llama pueda preguntar al usuario. Un árbol parcialmente imposible de analizar importa lo que puede y notifica el resto, en lugar de devolver una respuesta plausible pero errónea; la antigua ruta ``consolidate`` perdía en cambio imágenes sin ningún error.

A stitched field is one image with one name, so downstream modules do not need a tile axis. See :mod:`spacr.image_stitch` for how the placement is computed, and for what it does when the tiles cannot be aligned.
records.translation: La convención de nombres de archivo que leen los módulos principales es plate/well/T/field/L/A/Z/channel y no tiene posición para mosaicos, de modo que cuatro mosaicos de un campo de imagen producirían cuatro imágenes con un mismo nombre. Un campo unido es una imagen con un nombre, por lo que los módulos posteriores no necesitan un eje de mosaico. Consulte :mod:`spacr.image_stitch` para saber cómo se calcula la colocación y qué hace cuando los mosaicos no pueden alinearse.

records.context: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` measures fields in a :class:`multiprocessing.Pool`. Under ``fork`` (the Linux default) a worker inherits this module's registries from the parent and hooks registered with :func:`register_preprocessing_hook` work without additional setup. Under ``spawn`` / ``forkserver`` (Windows, macOS, or ``SPACR_START_METHOD``) a worker is a fresh interpreter that has never seen them, so an in-process registration would be a **silent no-op in every worker**. For that case set :data:`HOOKS_ENV_VAR`

records.source: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` measures fields in a :class:`multiprocessing.Pool`. Under ``fork`` (the Linux default) a worker inherits this module's registries from the parent and hooks registered with :func:`register_preprocessing_hook` work without additional setup. Under ``spawn`` / ``forkserver`` (Windows, macOS, or ``SPACR_START_METHOD``) a worker is a fresh interpreter that has never seen them, so an in-process registration would be a **silent no-op in every worker**. For that case set :data:`HOOKS_ENV_VAR`
records.translation: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` mide los campos de imagen en un :class:`multiprocessing.Pool`. Con ``fork`` (el valor por defecto en Linux), un proceso de trabajo hereda del proceso padre los registros de este módulo, y los ganchos registrados con :func:`register_preprocessing_hook` funcionan sin configuración adicional. Con ``spawn`` / ``forkserver`` (Windows, macOS o ``SPACR_START_METHOD``), un proceso de trabajo es un intérprete nuevo que nunca los ha visto, de modo que un registro dentro del proceso sería una **operación nula silenciosa en cada proceso de trabajo**. Para ese caso, establezca :data:`HOOKS_ENV_VAR`

records.context: A cell with four pathogens in it has four rows in ``pathogen`` and one in ``cell``. Putting a pathogen measurement on the same axis as a cell measurement means rolling those four up into one number -- and which number depends entirely on what is being measured:
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A cell with four pathogens in it has four rows in ``pathogen`` and one in ``cell``. Putting a pathogen measurement on the same axis as a cell measurement means rolling those four up into one number -- and which number depends entirely on what is being measured:
records.translation: Una célula con cuatro patógenos tiene cuatro filas en ``pathogen`` y una en ``cell``. Colocar una medición de patógeno en el mismo eje que una medición de célula implica reducir esas cuatro a un solo número, y qué número depende por completo de lo que se mide:

records.context: area, perimeter, integrated intensity, counts   -> SUM minimum intensity                               -> MIN of the four maximum intensity                               -> MAX of the four mean, median                                    -> the object mean/median shape descriptors, positions                    -> mean text                                            -> the first
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: area, perimeter, integrated intensity, counts   -> SUM minimum intensity                               -> MIN of the four maximum intensity                               -> MAX of the four mean, median                                    -> the object mean/median shape descriptors, positions                    -> mean text                                            -> the first
records.translation: área, perímetro, intensidad integrada, recuentos   -> SUM intensidad mínima                               -> MIN de las cuatro intensidad máxima                               -> MAX de las cuatro media, mediana                                    -> la media o mediana de los objetos descriptores de forma, posiciones                    -> media texto                                            -> el primero

records.context: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` already does this join, and aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``. That silently answers a different question per column: four pathogens' total area becomes an average area, a count becomes an average count, and a minimum becomes a mean of minima, which is not a minimum of anything. The join is otherwise sound -- it is where the parent link, the timelapse structured-data name and the cardinality checks live -- so this module changes what the aggregation is, not how the tables find each other.
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` already does this join, and aggregates every numeric column with ``mean``. That silently answers a different question per column: four pathogens' total area becomes an average area, a count becomes an average count, and a minimum becomes a mean of minima, which is not a minimum of anything. The join is otherwise sound -- it is where the parent link, the timelapse key and the cardinality checks live -- so this module changes what the aggregation is, not how the tables find each other.
records.translation: ``spacr.io._read_and_join_tables`` ya realiza esta unión y agrega cada columna numérica con ``mean``. Eso responde en silencio a una pregunta distinta para cada columna: el área total de cuatro patógenos se convierte en un área media, un recuento se convierte en un recuento medio y un mínimo se convierte en una media de mínimos, que no es el mínimo de nada. Por lo demás, la unión es correcta (es donde residen el vínculo con el progenitor, la clave de la serie temporal y las comprobaciones de cardinalidad), por lo que este módulo cambia en qué consiste la agregación, no cómo se encuentran las tablas entre sí.

records.context: **Naming.** A merged column carries its table: ``area`` from ``nucleus`` becomes ``nucleus_area``. Prefix rather than suffix so every column of one object sorts together in the axis picker, which is how anyone looks for them.
records.label: spacr.merge_tables#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Naming.** A merged column carries its table: ``area`` from ``nucleus`` becomes ``nucleus_area``. Prefix rather than suffix so every column of one object sorts together in the axis picker, which is how anyone looks for them.
records.translation: **Nomenclatura.** Una columna fusionada lleva su tabla: ``area`` de ``nucleus`` se convierte en ``nucleus_area``. Se usa un prefijo y no un sufijo para que todas las columnas de un objeto queden ordenadas juntas en el selector de ejes, que es donde cualquiera las busca.

records.translation: :mod:`spacr.artifacts` proporciona la procedencia y las comprobaciones de obsolescencia artefacto por artefacto: ``upstream_of`` / ``downstream_of`` recorren las aristas de procedencia desde un artefacto, y ``is_stale`` indica si un artefacto sigue correspondiendo a aquello a partir de lo que se generó. Un proyecto que se ha ejecutado, se ha vuelto a ejecutar en parte y de nuevo con otro diámetro de máscara contiene muchos artefactos, y la pregunta es cuáles de sus archivos siguen correspondiendo a sus entradas.

records.context: **Stale is not missing.** An artifact whose inputs moved on is stale — the number in it no longer follows from the files it names. An artifact that was deleted is missing — an availability problem. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` already refuses to conflate them and so does this: a node can be both, and the :attr:`Node.state` reports missing first because a file that is not there cannot be re-read to check anything else.
records.label: spacr.pipeline_graph#7

records.source: **Stale is not missing.** An artifact whose inputs moved on is stale — the number in it no longer follows from the files it names. An artifact that was deleted is missing — an availability problem. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` already refuses to conflate them and so does this: a node can be both, and the :attr:`Node.state` reports missing first because a file that is not there cannot be re-read to check anything else.
records.translation: **Obsoleto no es ausente.** Un artefacto cuyas entradas han cambiado está obsoleto: el número que contiene ya no se deduce de los archivos que nombra. Un artefacto que se eliminó está ausente: es un problema de disponibilidad. :mod:`spacr.artifacts` ya se niega a confundirlos, y este módulo también: un nodo puede ser ambas cosas, y :attr:`Node.state` notifica primero la ausencia porque un archivo que no está no puede volver a leerse para comprobar nada más.

records.context: **The registry is not the only source of truth.** A project can have run nothing at all, and a graph of zero nodes tells that user nothing. So :func:`module_graph` draws the *static* DAG from :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` — what feeds what, by declaration — and :func:`build_graph` records which modules of it have actually produced something. The application view shows the module DAG behind the artifact DAG for exactly that reason: an empty project still gets a picture of the workflow it is about to execute.

records.source: **The registry is not the only source of truth.** A project can have run nothing at all, and a graph of zero nodes tells that user nothing. So :func:`module_graph` draws the *static* DAG from :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` — what feeds what, by declaration — and :func:`build_graph` records which modules of it have actually produced something. The screen shows the module DAG behind the artifact DAG for exactly that reason: an empty project still gets a picture of the pipeline it is about to run.
records.translation: **El registro no es la única fuente de verdad.** Un proyecto puede no haber ejecutado nada, y un grafo de cero nodos no le dice nada a ese usuario. Por ello, :func:`module_graph` dibuja el DAG *estático* a partir de :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` (qué alimenta a qué, por declaración) y :func:`build_graph` registra qué módulos de él han producido realmente algo. La pantalla muestra el DAG de módulos detrás del DAG de artefactos exactamente por ese motivo: un proyecto vacío sigue obteniendo una imagen de la cadena de procesamiento que está a punto de ejecutar.

Este último conjunto se recalcula recorriendo de nuevo ``AGGREGATION_RULES`` (:func:`default_aggregated_columns`) en lugar de enumerarse en algún lugar, de modo que no puede desincronizarse de las reglas.

records.context: The module handles three issues:
records.label: spacr.profiler#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The module handles three issues:
records.translation: El módulo aborda tres cuestiones:

records.context: **The regression backends predict differently.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` spans statsmodels results (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, four GLM families, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), scikit-learn estimators (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) and the horseshoe fitter. :func:`predict` is the one call that works on all of them, and :func:`response_scale` names what came back — because a GLM-binomial returns a probability, a Poisson GLM returns a rate, and ``LinearSVC.predict`` returns a class label, which would draw a step function and look like a finding. The hinge backend is profiled through ``decision_function`` for exactly that reason, and the scale says so.
records.label: spacr.profiler#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The regression backends predict differently.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` spans statsmodels results (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, four GLM families, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), scikit-learn estimators (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) and the horseshoe fitter. :func:`predict` is the one call that works on all of them, and :func:`response_scale` names what came back — because a GLM-binomial returns a probability, a Poisson GLM returns a rate, and ``LinearSVC.predict`` returns a CLASS LABEL, which would draw a step function and look like a finding. The hinge backend is profiled through ``decision_function`` for exactly that reason, and the scale says so.
records.translation: **Los motores de regresión predicen de forma distinta.** :data:`spacr.ml.REGRESSION_TYPES` abarca resultados de statsmodels (``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, cuatro familias GLM, ``QuantReg``, ``MixedLM``, ``BetaModel``), estimadores de scikit-learn (``Lasso``, ``Ridge``, ``ElasticNet``, ``LinearSVC``) y el ajustador horseshoe. :func:`predict` es la única llamada que funciona con todos ellos, y :func:`response_scale` nombra lo que se devolvió, porque un GLM binomial devuelve una probabilidad, un GLM de Poisson devuelve una tasa y ``LinearSVC.predict`` devuelve una ETIQUETA DE CLASE, que dibujaría una función escalonada y parecería un hallazgo. Precisamente por eso, el motor hinge se perfila mediante ``decision_function``, y la escala lo indica.

records.context: **Nothing here re-fits.** The model handed in is the model profiled. A profiler that quietly re-fits is showing the user a second model and labelling it the first, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` the second one is not even the same model. Where a caller has only the written-out coefficients and no live object, :func:`from_coefficients` builds a :class:`FittedLinear` around them — that is *reading* the fit, not repeating it, and the class says which link it is applying.
records.label: spacr.profiler#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Nothing here re-fits.** The model handed in is the model profiled. A profiler that quietly re-fits is showing the user a second model and labelling it the first, and on a penalised backend with ``alpha='auto'`` the second one is not even the same model. Where a caller has only the written-out coefficients and no live object, :func:`from_coefficients` builds a :class:`FittedLinear` around them — that is *reading* the fit, not repeating it, and the class says which link it is applying.
records.translation: **Aquí no se vuelve a ajustar nada.** El modelo que se entrega es el modelo que se perfila. Un perfilador que vuelve a ajustar discretamente muestra al usuario un segundo modelo con la etiqueta del primero, y en un motor penalizado con ``alpha='auto'`` el segundo ni siquiera es el mismo modelo. Cuando quien llama solo tiene los coeficientes escritos y ningún objeto activo, :func:`from_coefficients` construye un :class:`FittedLinear` en torno a ellos: eso es *leer* el ajuste, no repetirlo, y la clase indica qué función de enlace aplica.

records.context: **A held value is a choice, not a default.** :func:`reference_row` picks the median of each column and is explicit that it did; the ``at`` argument overrides any of them; and every :class:`Profile` carries the full held vector, so a curve can always be traced back to the assumptions that produced it.
records.label: spacr.profiler#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A held value is a choice, not a default.** :func:`reference_row` picks the median of each column and is explicit that it did; the ``at`` argument overrides any of them; and every :class:`Profile` carries the full held vector, so a curve can always be traced back to the assumptions that produced it.
records.translation: **Un valor fijado es una elección, no un valor por defecto.** :func:`reference_row` elige la mediana de cada columna e indica explícitamente que lo hizo; el argumento ``at`` sustituye cualquiera de ellas; y cada :class:`Profile` lleva el vector completo de valores fijados, de modo que una curva siempre puede rastrearse hasta los supuestos que la produjeron.

records.context: The order the branches are tried in is load-bearing:
records.label: spacr.profiler.predict#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The order the branches are tried in is load-bearing:
records.translation: El orden en que se prueban las ramas es fundamental:

records.context: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (the ``hinge`` backend) has both that and ``predict``, and its ``predict`` returns a 0/1 CLASS. A profile of a class label is a step function, which reads as a finding and is an artefact of asking the wrong method. 2. a statsmodels results object — ``predict(exog)`` applies the inverse link, so a GLM comes back on the response scale. ``offset`` is passed when the object accepts one. 3. anything else with ``predict`` — the scikit-learn regressors. 4. the linear predictor from ``params`` / ``coef_``, for a fitted object that carries coefficients and nothing else (the horseshoe fitter).
records.label: spacr.profiler.predict#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. ``decision_function`` — ``LinearSVC`` (the ``hinge`` backend) has both that and ``predict``, and its ``predict`` returns a 0/1 CLASS. A profile of a class label is a step function, which reads as a finding and is an artefact of asking the wrong method. 2. a statsmodels results object — ``predict(exog)`` applies the inverse link, so a GLM comes back on the response scale. ``offset`` is passed when the object accepts one. 3. anything else with ``predict`` — the scikit-learn regressors. 4. the linear predictor from ``params`` / ``coef_``, for a fitted object that carries coefficients and nothing else (the horseshoe fitter).
records.translation: 1. ``decision_function``: ``LinearSVC`` (el motor ``hinge``) tiene tanto ese método como ``predict``, y su ``predict`` devuelve una CLASE 0/1. El perfil de una etiqueta de clase es una función escalonada, que se interpreta como un hallazgo y es un artefacto de llamar al método equivocado. 2. un objeto de resultados de statsmodels: ``predict(exog)`` aplica la función de enlace inversa, de modo que un GLM se devuelve en la escala de la respuesta. Se pasa ``offset`` cuando el objeto lo acepta. 3. cualquier otro objeto con ``predict``: los regresores de scikit-learn. 4. el predictor lineal a partir de ``params`` / ``coef_``, para un objeto ajustado que solo lleva coeficientes (el ajustador horseshoe).

records.source: No command uses ``shell=True``.  SSH necessarily invokes a remote login shell; all user-controlled values interpolated into its small fixed scripts are quoted with :func:`shlex.quote`, and host names are validated separately. Custom command profiles are parsed into argument vectors and substitute each placeholder inside one argument, so shell operators have no special meaning.
records.translation: Ningún comando usa ``shell=True``.
